title: Workflow Definition
description: Complete JSON Schema for a workflow stored in PGC_Workflow.steps. Authoritative source: docs/architecture.md sections 6.5.1–6.5.5. Used by generate_workflow_steps and design_workflow_dialogs LLM prompts to validate generated output.

name.description: snake_case unique workflow identifier. Matches PGC_Workflow.name.

domain.description: PGD domain this workflow belongs to. Null for system-level workflows.

description.description: One-sentence description for workflow authors and right-brain LLM context.

version.description: Monotonically incrementing version. Managed by upsert-workflow.mjs — do not set manually.

was_successful.description: Outcome of the last probe run. Null until first probe.

state_strategy.description: 'sequential' — advance automatically. 'sequential_with_confirmation' — pause for user confirmation between steps.

model_used.description: LLM model that generated this workflow. Informational only.

intent_keywords.description: Natural language phrases used for Pass 2 LLM intent classification.

steps.description: Ordered step array. Step keys are arbitrary strings ('1', '3a', '5b'). Must include at least one 'end' step. The Step Processor resolves keys by string equality — parseInt is never used.

routingToken.description: Valid routing value for on_success, on_else, on_select, on_complete. Canonical values: 'next' (advance to next step), 'end' (complete run), 'cancel' (cancel run), or a bare step key (e.g. '3', '3a', '1R'). step:N format is also accepted for backwards compatibility. SYNC NOTE: this pattern must be kept identical to the routingToken pattern inside PGC_Prompt.output_schema for generate_workflow_steps (seed_PGC_Prompt.json). When updating either, update both.

bareStepKey.description: Used in condition.on_success and condition.on_else. Bare step key — same rule as all other routing fields. Do NOT use routing tokens (next, end, cancel) here — they will fail at runtime because condition routes to a step key, not a control token.

modalDescriptor.description: Attached to an option or special_button. Clicking the button opens a Slack overlay modal without advancing the workflow. The workflow stays suspended at the current gate. Only modal submission (handleViewSubmission) enqueues resume_gate.

input_label.description: Label above the text input in the modal.

placeholder.description: Placeholder text in the modal input.

multiline.description: True renders a textarea; false renders a single-line input.

filterItem.description: Single WHERE clause condition for serv_query, serv_update, serv_delete. 'value' supports {{template}} substitution against local_state. Omit 'value' for null-check ops (is_null, not_null).

op.description: eq=equals, ne=not-equals, like=SQL LIKE, in=IN(array), is_null/not_null=null check (no value needed), jsonb_contains/jsonb_contained_by=JSONB @>/<@ containment

value.description: Supports {{template}} substitution. Use a string for most operators. Use an array of strings for op: 'in'. Use an object or array of objects for op: 'jsonb_contains'/'jsonb_contained_by' — matched via Postgres @>/<@ containment, not string comparison. Omit for is_null/not_null.

confirmOption.description: Option shape for confirm, list_selection, review_object, and text_input gate types. Uses 'action' (not 'value') as the machine identifier.

label.description: Button text shown to the user.

action.description: Machine identifier matched by resume_gate. 'confirm' and 'cancel' are conventional values.

on_modal_close.description: Routing when this option's modal is dismissed without submitting. Defaults to on_select.

output_key.description: Option-level output_key. When this option carries a modal, the modal inputValue is written to this local_state key on submit — instead of the parent step's output_key.

choiceOption.description: Option shape for choice gate types. Uses 'value' (not 'action') as the machine identifier. 'value' is written to output_key on selection (or replaced by modal inputValue if a modal was submitted).

label.description: Short button text — typically a single letter (A, B, C) or short word.

value.description: Machine identifier written to output_key. Used by resume_gate to match the user's selection.

description.description: Explanatory sentence displayed above the buttons in the Slack message.

output_key.description: Option-level output_key. When this option carries a modal, the modal inputValue is written to this local_state key on modal submit — instead of the parent step's output_key.

specialButton.description: Button appended AFTER options in the Slack actions block. Never appears in description_list or other content fields. Use for: Cancel (so it does not appear in the option description list), Other/Skip buttons, modal triggers. Field convention: use 'value' for choice gates; use 'action' for all other gate types (confirm, text_input, list_selection, review_object).

value.description: Machine identifier for choice gate special_buttons.

action.description: Machine identifier for non-choice gate special_buttons.

on_modal_close.description: Routing when this button's modal is dismissed without submitting.

style.description: Slack button style. Omitting defaults to 'default'.

output_key.description: Writes modal inputValue to this local_state key on modal submit.

formField.description: One value collected by a form gate. `type` states WHAT is being collected, never which widget draws it — the experience layer maps 'date' to a Slack datepicker, 'select' to a dropdown, and so on. A new widget is therefore never a new gate_type.

name.description: Key this field's answer takes in the object written to output_key.

type.description: What to collect. select/radio hold one value; multi_select/checkbox write an ARRAY. date yields 'YYYY-MM-DD', time 'HH:mm'. radio and checkbox are capped at 10 options by Slack; select and multi_select at 100 — above that, collect the value another way. (number/email/url/file are deliberately absent: Slack supports them only in modals, so collect text and validate in a js_transform.)

label.description: Shown above the input. Supports {{template}} substitution. Defaults to `name`.

placeholder.description: Hint shown inside an empty input.

optional.description: True lets the user submit without answering — the field arrives as null. Required fields are enforced on submit; a gap re-renders the gate rather than advancing.

default.description: Pre-filled value, shown in the input before the user edits it. For date, an ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string; for select/radio, the `value` of the option to pre-select. Use it to let a user amend an existing record rather than retype it.

options.description: select/multi_select/radio/checkbox: a fixed option list, authored inline. Each entry is { value, label } or a bare string. Use options_key instead when the choices are data.

options_key.description: Dot-path into local_state holding the option rows — lets a dropdown offer data the workflow just queried (e.g. the categories it loaded) instead of a hardcoded list. This is what makes a deterministic pick possible where free text would otherwise need an llm_call to parse.

option_value_key.description: Field on each options_key row supplying the option's value.

option_label_key.description: Field on each options_key row supplying the option's visible label.

itemAction.description: Selection action for list_selection gates, applied uniformly to every item unless an item already carries its own secondaryAction. Rendering is always the same (one markdown table for all rows, one shared selection control, one Select button labeled/styled from this config); what the action does is entirely up to the calling workflow, expressed here, not by a different gate_type.

condition.description: JS expression evaluated against each item. Items where falsy are still listed but are not selectable.

action.description: Any caller-chosen action name (e.g. 'select_row', 'view_record'). Selecting a row writes it to the step's output_key and advances via on_select (below); the action name itself carries no special behaviour.

action_data_key.description: Field on the item written to responseData. Typically 'tableName' (the historical name — carries whatever id/value the selected row needs, regardless of action).

confirm_template.description: Slack mrkdwn shown in a confirmation dialog before the action fires. Supports {{item.field}} placeholders. Computed by buildDialog but currently has no renderer — the shared Select button has no row bound to it until after submission.

style.description: Button style. No default. 'default' is never sent to Slack (no such enum value there) — omitted entirely so the button renders with no special emphasis.

on_select.description: Required. Routing target when a row is selected (e.g. drill-down). Resolved directly — NOT via a matching entry in options[], since every options[] entry also renders as its own visible bottom button (which would duplicate it).

step.description: A single workflow instruction. Discriminated by 'type'. Step keys are arbitrary strings — the Step Processor resolves them by string equality.

llmCallStep.description: Loads a prompt from PGC_Prompt by intent_category key, calls the LLM, and runs review-output.mjs validation (2-attempt correction loop). Right-brain hooks are wired in by the Step Processor — no workflow changes needed.

prompt.description: PGC_Prompt.intent_category key — must match an existing row.

input.description: All fields other than 'prompt' are passed as template variables into the LLM prompt text via {{variable}} substitution.

output_key.description: local_state key where the parsed LLM JSON response is written.

save_to_memory.description: When present, the harness appends a reasoning instruction to the prompt, strips the 'reasoning' field from the LLM output before validation, and writes it to PGC_Memory. Step never fails if the memory write fails.

scope.description: Scope keys (domain, workflow, topic). May contain {{template}} tokens resolved against local_state.

jsTransformStep.description: Evaluates a synchronous JS expression in a sandboxed vm.runInNewContext context. Restricted to pure data transformation — no I/O, no async, no require. Timeout: 200ms.

input_key.description: Dot-path into local_state. Resolved value is available as 'items' in the sandbox. Required if the expression reads 'items'.

expression.description: Synchronous JS value expression. Available bindings: 'items' (resolved input_key value), 'local_state' (full state object), JSON, Math, Array, Object, String, Number, Boolean, Date. No 'return' keyword at top level — expression must evaluate to a value. Wrap multi-statement logic in an IIFE: (function(){ ... })(). Forbidden: require, import, process, global, await, async, eval, fetch, new Function.

output_key.description: Dot-path into local_state where the expression result is written.

system_key.description: Optional. Identifies a PGC_SystemContext key whose content is injected as 'system' binding in the sandbox.

max_rows.description: Optional. Caps the number of rows returned when the expression produces an array. Applied after the expression evaluates.

root_only.description: Optional. When true, strips child arrays from entity result objects before writing to output_key.

humanGateStep.description: Suspends the workflow stack and presents a Slack dialog. Resumes when the user responds via /interactive. Gate type determines the dialog shape, option schema, and what is written to output_key. Options must include at least one cancel path.

gate_type.description: Determines dialog rendering and option shape. confirm: typography + buttons. list_selection: one markdown table of every context_key item (pre-formatted as { id, fields?, secondaryAction? } — fields is a plain object of column name -> value, rendered as one table column per distinct key across every item, sparse where an item lacks a given key), plus one shared selection control and one Select button. item_action applies uniformly to every item unless an item already carries its own secondaryAction. The selection control is a dropdown of every selectable row — grouped by source table when a level spans more than one — falling back to a plain id text box past Slack's 100-option cap; the user picks a row and clicks Select, and resumeGate resolves the selection back to that row. What selecting does (mutate this list and stay suspended vs write the row's id and advance elsewhere, e.g. Sprint 7 Track D2 drill-down) is driven entirely by item_action's own config (action name + on_select), never by this gate_type name — rendering and behavior are deliberately decoupled. form: collects any number of typed values in ONE gate — see `fields`. Each field declares WHAT it collects (text, select, multi_select, radio, checkbox, date, time, datetime) and the experience layer picks the widget, so a new input type never needs a new gate_type. The answers are written to output_key as one object keyed by field name. Reach for a form whenever the values are enumerable, a date, or otherwise structured: a picker is deterministic, whereas a text_input followed by an llm_call to parse the free text is not, and can misread the user. text_input: inline Slack input block — a single free-text answer, for genuinely unstructured prose only. review_object: key/value display. choice: lettered buttons with descriptions; the click itself routes (each option has its own on_select), so use it for a branch decision, not to capture data. followup_prompt: notification with Ask follow-up modal button.

message_template.description: Slack mrkdwn displayed above the dialog. Supports {{key}}, {{key.field}}, {{key.0.field}}, {{item.field}} (inside iterator only), {{input.field}} template substitution. Resolved at suspension time against local_state.

output_key.description: Required for text_input (written on Submit) and choice (written on selection or modal submit). The typed modal text (inputValue) takes precedence over the button value for choice gates with modal options. On a form gate it holds the FIELD VALUES — not which button was pressed; use action_key for that.

action_key.description: local_state key recording WHICH option the user chose (an option's value on choice gates, its action on all others). Use it when a later step must know the gate's outcome — most commonly a save-and-continue loop, where 'Save' and 'Done' run the SAME write and only diverge afterwards, so the decision must survive the write. Every option must then carry a DISTINCT action (e.g. 'save', 'done', 'cancel'): reusing the conventional 'confirm' on two buttons makes them indistinguishable to everything downstream. Independent of output_key — a form gate uses both.

context_key.description: Dot-path into local_state. Required for list_selection (must resolve to an array, pre-formatted as { id, fields?, secondaryAction? } — building that shape is a preceding js_transform's job, not this gate's) and review_object (resolves to object or array). Optional for confirm with dynamic button list.

item_primary_key.description: review_object array mode: fallback single-field label. Defaults to 'tableName'.

item_secondary_key.description: review_object array mode: value field. Defaults to 'columns'.

item_label_template.description: review_object array mode: template for the row label, e.g. 'step {{step}} — {{field}}'. Resolved against each array item's own properties.

fields.description: form only, and required for it. One entry per value to collect. The whole form is answered in one gate and written to output_key as a single object keyed by field name, e.g. { period: '2026-07-01', category_id: '3' }. Collect enumerable values, dates and structured input here rather than gathering free text and parsing it with an llm_call — a picker is deterministic, parsing prose is not. May instead be a {{state_key}} reference to an array a preceding js_transform built, exactly as `options` and `reveals` may be: that is how a form carries one field per data row (an amount box and a type dropdown for each budget category, say), which a fixed field list cannot express.

input_label.description: text_input only. Short label shown above the Slack input element. Defaults to 'Your input'. Full instructions go in message_template.

multiline.description: text_input only. True renders a multi-line textarea; false renders a single-line input.

placeholder.description: text_input only. Placeholder text shown inside the Slack input element when empty. Supports newlines for multiline hints.

options.description: Gate action buttons. Shape is determined by gate_type: choice gates use choiceOption (value field, not action); all other gate types use confirmOption (action field, not value). Must include at least one cancel path — either here or in special_buttons. Supports an inline array or a {{template}} reference to a local_state array of the same shape (e.g. a level-dependent button set computed by a preceding js_transform) — when templated, the cancel-path requirement is enforced via on_cancel instead, since static analysis cannot inspect the eventual contents.

special_buttons.description: Appended after options in the Slack actions block. Never rendered in description_list. Field convention: choice gates use 'value'; non-choice gates use 'action'. Any button may carry a modal descriptor to open an overlay without advancing the workflow.

reveal.description: Optional single collapsible container block shown above the gate buttons. Does NOT advance or resume the gate.

content.description: Template reference (e.g. {{key}}) resolving to a string, array of strings, or array of plain record objects. Strings render via basic mrkdwn; an array of plain records auto-renders as a real Slack table — see docs/slack-block-kit.md.

reveals.description: Array version of reveal — renders one collapsible container per entry (e.g. one per table). Supports an inline array or a {{template}} reference to a local_state array of {button_label, content} objects.

on_cancel.description: Routing when the user cancels. Use "cancel" to end the workflow immediately, or a step key (e.g. "step:cleanup") to route to a cleanup step first.

servSchemaStep.description: Creates a PGD table via SERV /schema/createTable. Typically used inside a non-suspending iterator to create tables from an array of table definition objects.

input.description: Full table definition object (tableName, columns, etc.), or a template string resolving to one. Use '{{item}}' inside an iterator to pass each array element.

table.description: Template resolving to a table definition object. Typically '{{item}}' inside an iterator.

servQueryStep.description: SELECT rows from a PGD or PGC table via SERV. For domains with child tables, prefer serv_entity_query.

tableName.description: Mixed-case table name without SQL quotes — SERV adds them.

servInsertStep.description: INSERT one row into a PGD or PGC table via SERV. Table must be registered in PGC_TableMap with allow_insert: true. Never include id, created_at, or updated_at in the row.

row.description: Column key/value pairs, or a {{template}} string resolving to an object at runtime (e.g. '{{generated.domainHelp}}'). Do not include id, created_at, updated_at.

ref_fk_columns.description: Optional. Array of ref FK descriptors from serv_entity_schema. When present and row is an array, each FK column with a string value is resolved to an integer ID before insert.

output_key.description: Optional. Receives the inserted row if provided.

servUpdateStep.description: UPDATE matching rows in a PGD or PGC table via SERV. Enforces non-empty filters — will refuse to update without a WHERE clause.

updates.description: Column key/value pairs to SET, or a {{template}} string resolving to an object at runtime (e.g. '{{input.updates}}').

servDeleteStep.description: DELETE matching rows from a PGD or PGC table via SERV. Enforces non-empty filters — will refuse to delete without a WHERE clause.

servEntityQueryStep.description: LIST assembled entities via SERV Entity. Returns root columns plus jsonb_agg child arrays. Use instead of serv_query for domains with child tables or when a full entity display is needed.

entityName.description: PascalCase singular name from PGC_EntitySchema.entity_name (e.g. 'Recipe', not 'Recipes').

servEntityGetStep.description: FETCH a single assembled entity by id via SERV Entity. Returns root columns plus all child arrays.

servEntitySchemaStep.description: Loads a full entity schema by joining PGC_EntitySchema (topology) with PGC_Schema (live column definitions). Replaces the two-step serv_query + js_transform pattern. Use when a workflow needs to know the entity's join structure and column list at runtime.

output_key.description: Receives { entity_name, description, root: { table, columns }, children: [{ table, alias, fk_column, parent, match_by, columns }] }.

servEntityInsertStep.description: Inserts a multi-level entity in topological order with automatic FK threading. Handles n-level hierarchies and self-referential tables. Use after serv_entity_schema + parse_entity_input.

entitySchema.description: {{template}} resolving to entity schema from serv_entity_schema output.

parsedEntity.description: {{template}} resolving to parsed entity from parse_entity_input llm_call output.

conditionStep.description: Evaluates a {{template}} expression against local_state and routes to on_success or on_else. Produces no output — no output_key. Truthy: resolved value is non-empty, not 'null', not 'undefined', not '0', and contains no unresolved {{ markers.

on_success.description: Step key to route to when expression is truthy. Bare key only — do NOT prefix with 'step:'.

on_else.description: Step key to route to when expression is falsy. Bare key only — do NOT prefix with 'step:'.

iteratorStep.description: Loops over an array in local_state, executing item_step for each element. Non-suspending when item_step is a service step (all items in one Lambda invocation). Suspending when item_step is human_gate (one SQS round-trip per item). execution_mode must always be 'sequential' — omitting it is a workflow defect.

items_key.description: Dot-path to an array in local_state.

item_step.description: Step definition executed for each item. The current item is bound as '{{item}}' and '{{item.field}}' in all template strings and input fields. Results are collected at output_key.

output_key.description: Collects each item_step result into an array written to this local_state key.

on_complete.description: Routing after all items are processed. Accepts a routingToken (next, end, step:N) or a bare step key (e.g. '5a') — the executor resolves bare keys the same way as condition.on_success.

notifyStep.description: Resolves message_template from local_state and enqueues a HUMAN_NOTIFICATION message to the callback channel (Slack thread). Does not suspend the workflow.

message_template.description: Slack mrkdwn. Supports {{template}} substitution against local_state.

reveal.description: Optional single collapsible panel below the message content (Sprint 7 Track D2).

content.description: Template reference (e.g. {{key}}) resolving to a string, array of strings, or array of plain record objects. Strings render via basic mrkdwn; an array of plain records auto-renders as a real Slack table — see docs/slack-block-kit.md.

reveals.description: Array version of reveal — renders one panel per entry. Supports an inline array or a {{template}} reference to a local_state array of {button_label, content} objects.

simulateStep.description: Dry-runs a workflow step array against named execution paths using injected mock outputs. Three validation levels: (1) static analysis — step key uniqueness, routing target existence, required fields; (2) path execution — traces each named path through the step graph; (3) skip-path analysis — detects unreachable steps. on_else routes back to the step where the user can correct the workflow before re-simulating.

steps_key.description: Dot-path to the draft workflow steps array in local_state.

mock_outputs_key.description: Optional. Dot-path to mock output map. If absent, only Level 1 static analysis runs.

paths_key.description: Optional. Dot-path to simulation paths array. If absent, only Level 1 static analysis runs.

skeleton.description: Optional. Set to true when simulating a routing skeleton. Skips serv_step_missing_required_input — content fields are not yet present. All routing topology checks still run.

locked_skeleton_key.description: Optional. Dot-path to the routing skeleton this step array was translated from. When present, L1 checks that translation emitted exactly one step per design item and invented none of its own (skeleton_drift). The step set is locked once the skeleton is validated; only the design stage may add a step.

output_key.description: Receives the simulation result: { passed, issues, paths_executed }.

writeMemoryStep.description: Persists a PGC_Memory row. Content is read from local_state[content_key]. Never fails the run — errors are logged only.

content_key.description: Key in local_state whose string value is written as the memory content.

endStep.description: Marks the workflow run as completed and stops execution. Every workflow must include exactly one end step.
